A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUE research, with matching authors, method, and core experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, component ablations, image-generation examples, zero-shot classification, and cross-domain classification in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Handwritten retrieval, CSA and SAIL comparisons, mAP results, and a GTR encoder experiment.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same independent SpectralNet embeddings, paired CCA alignment, residual MMD alignment, and inference mappings. Graph construction and training objectives are unchanged. The added encoder experiment and feature-extraction disclosures do not establish a revision to SUE.

E1.justification: v2 adds Handwritten retrieval between KL coefficients and pixel averages, described as two handcrafted image-derived feature sets without pretrained encoders (Tables 1 and 12). This is a bounded coverage extension; the existing vision-language, vision-vision, generation, zero-shot, and cross-domain tasks remain.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands retrieval comparisons by adding CSA across Table 1 and SAIL on MSCOCO, Flickr30k, and Polyvore in Appendix A.2/Table 4. These supplement the retained Contrastive and MMD comparisons with methods positioned for limited paired data or incorporating unpaired data.

E3.justification: v2 adds mAP evaluation under the Table 1 settings and tests a GTR T5-large text-encoder configuration. The original 400-example retrieval evaluation, data preparation, validation splits, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Newly specified pooling and token selection are disclosures rather than demonstrated protocol changes.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6/Table 8 extends encoder sensitivity analysis with GTR, testing whether a larger alternative text encoder improves alignment. The component and autoencoder ablations, paired/unpaired sample analyses, qualitative examples, and modality-gap visualizations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and shaded bands in Figures 5 and 8. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, explanations of the bands, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: Matched existing results remain unchanged, but v2 substantially expands reported outcomes with CSA and SAIL scores, mAP across five datasets, Handwritten retrieval, and GTR results. Examples include Handwritten SUE R@10 of 79.00 and 78.00 in Table 1 and GTR R@10 of 31.25 in Table 8. These are additional results, not improvements to unchanged SUE configurations.

T1.justification: New Appendix D explicitly states the cited Bérard et al. theorem, including metric-perturbation and Ricci-curvature assumptions and a finite-eigenfunction sup-norm bound. v1 provides only the prose motivation and citation in Section 4.1. This adds formal detail, but no new proof or SUE-specific guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: shared representations from almost exclusively unpaired data, spectral embeddings as the basis for universality, and SUE's three-stage construction. The claimed MSCOCO improvement over contrastive learning is unchanged; the additional experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses for GTR's weaker performance, attributes the claimed absence of a modality gap to CCA centering and MMD, and explicitly identifies generalization to video, speech, and scientific data as unresolved. The existing qualification about not matching heavily paired state-of-the-art models is retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 newly specifies Sentence-Transformers mean pooling and DINOv2 CLS-token extraction; Table 12 documents Handwritten's feature inputs and sample counts. Appendix A changes future code availability to an available repository, resolving its inconsistency with v1's abstract, which already linked the code. v2 also supplies a project-page link.

R1.justification: Related work adds a short distinction from CSA and citations to SAIL, OmniBind, and interventional-consistency alignment. References for Handwritten and GTR are also added. The overall research positioning and novelty claims remain stable; publication-metadata and citation-style updates do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local changes include a labeled limitations paragraph, new appendix subsections, expanded terminology, revised cross-references, an additional author affiliation, and numbered citations. This is a limited narrative revision rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The paper is reformatted into NeurIPS style with narrower text and figure widths and changed headers and typography. Table 1 gains CSA columns, Handwritten rows, and shading; new SAIL and mAP tables are added. Appendix figures are extensively regrouped, including Figures 8–12 together, while their underlying content is retained.

improvement.justification: CSA and SAIL comparisons address v1's limited comparator coverage, while the added benchmark, metric, and encoder test broaden empirical support. Feature-extraction details and consistent code-access statements improve reproducibility. The gains are incremental: uncertainty reporting remains unchanged, and the conflicting CCA budgets—600 pairs in Appendix E.8 versus dataset-specific counts in Table 1—remain unresolved.
